title: Security in System Design
intro: Embed zero-trust defense-in-depth principles across all architectural tiers, encompassing network boundaries, cryptographic identity, and data protection.
objectives: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) and SPIFFE identities for service-to-service communication.
Validate stateless JWT tokens with asymmetric public key cryptography (RS256/EdDSA).
Mitigate OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQLi, XSS, SSRF) using Web Application Firewalls (WAF).
body:
### Defense-in-Depth Tiers
1. **Edge & Ingress**: Cloudflare / AWS WAF filtering SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and Layer 7 volumetric DDoS attacks.
2. **Network Perimeter**: Private VPC subnets. Database nodes placed in private isolated subnets with zero public internet IP addresses.
3. **Service Mesh Zero-Trust**: Never trust internal datacenter networks. Enforce **Mutual TLS (mTLS)**: both client and server authenticate each other using x509 cryptographic certificates.
4. **Authentication & Authorization**: API Gateway validates OAuth2 / OIDC JSON Web Tokens (JWT). Asymmetric signing (RS256) allows microservices to verify authenticity using public keys without querying a centralized auth database.
5. **Data Protection**: Encryption at rest (AES-256 with AWS KMS envelope encryption) and column-level encryption for sensitive PII (credit cards, social security numbers).
keyIdea: Assume internal network compromise. Enforce zero-trust with mTLS, sign APIs with HMAC/JWT, and encrypt sensitive data both in transit and at rest.

concepts.title: Envelope Encryption
concepts.body: Encrypting plaintext data with a unique Data Encryption Key (DEK), and encrypting the DEK with a master Key Encryption Key (KEK) managed in HSM hardware.

concepts.title: HMAC Request Signing
concepts.body: Clients sign request payloads with a shared secret (`HMAC-SHA256(payload, secret)`). Prevents replay attacks and data tampering in transit.

examples: Istio service mesh automating mTLS certificate rotation across Kubernetes pods.

quiz.prompt: Why is asymmetric JWT signing (RS256) superior to symmetric signing (HS256) in microservice architectures?
options: Downstream microservices can verify tokens using the public key without needing access to the secret private key
HS256 requires internet access to verify
quiz.explanation: With RS256, only the auth server holds the private signing key. Microservices verify signatures using the public key, so a compromised service cannot forge tokens.
